title: Protecting Access to the Courts for Taxpayers Act
official_summary:
Protecting Access to the Courts for Taxpayers Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the federal judicial code to authorize a U.S. district court, a U.S. court of appeals, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, or the Court of International Trade to transfer to the U.S. Tax Court a misfiled case within the Tax Court's jurisdiction.

summary.headline: A 2018 law lets federal courts send a wrongly filed tax case to the U.S. Tax Court instead of dismissing it.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the federal judicial code. It lets a U.S. district court, a U.S. court of appeals, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, or the Court of International Trade transfer a case to the U.S. Tax Court when the case was filed in the wrong court but belongs in the Tax Court. The summary provided does not describe other changes in detail.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who file a tax case in the wrong federal court
who_it_affects.how: Their case can be moved to the Tax Court rather than being thrown out, which may help them avoid losing time or missing deadlines.

who_it_affects.group: Federal courts and the U.S. Tax Court
who_it_affects.how: These courts now have authority to transfer misfiled tax cases between them.
